findings.evidence: attribute_quotes uses bare `name_lower in context` substring match; reproduced Ann matching inside 'annual' and claiming the quote.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/voice_card_detector.py:117 — Substring speaker attribution. Authors are hurt: a name embedded in unrelated text can claim a quote, producing a false mismatch for the wrong character and omitting the real speaker.

findings.evidence: _KIND_PRIORITY ranks cross_chapter last (5); sort is severity then kind_rank then -count, so a 40-row cap can be filled by per-chapter kinds and emit zero cross_chapter rows.
findings.message: ghostreader/report/thrash_export.py:75 — Cross-chapter finding starvation. Users can receive no cross_chapter rows when the 40-row cap is filled by higher-priority per-chapter findings.

findings.evidence: _is_taught only requires the term and any _TEACH_IN_RE cue somewhere in the ±2-sentence neighborhood, not that the cue glosses that term, so unrelated parentheticals can mark coined terms taught.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/register_detector.py:150 — Term-to-gloss attribution is too broad. Users relying on jargon-earn findings can have unrelated nearby explanations mark a coined term as taught, undercounting unexplained terms and hiding a budget overrun.

findings.evidence: aggregate_cross_chapter never mixes within_scene in ch1 with chapter_rare in ch2; after within_keys drops ch1 rare, orphan rollup needs ≥2 rare chapters, so cross_chapter is omitted (reproduced).
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/thrash_detector.py:860 — Cross-chapter evidence loss. Authors relying on cross_chapter rows lose chapter-2 evidence when a lemma has a within_scene row in chapter 1 but only repeats across scenes in chapter 2.

findings.evidence: _candidate_ngrams allows gap<=2, so 'dark. Stone' (gap 2) counts as phrase 'dark stone'; detect_phrase_thrash reproduced count=3 on cross-sentence repeats.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/phrase_thrash.py:190-216 — Sentence-boundary phrase false positives. Writers can receive phrase-thrash findings for sequences such as “dark. Stone” that never occur as a contiguous phrase.

findings.evidence: attribute_quotes does name_to_slug[alias]=slug with no collision check, so a later cast member sharing a given-name alias overwrites the speaker map.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/voice_card_detector.py:101-104 — Alias collision. Authors are hurt: shared given-name aliases overwrite the speaker map, misattributing one character’s speech and potentially hiding their mismatch.

findings.evidence: _norm_token strips one trailing 's' only, so fox→fox and foxes→foxe; 'silver fox' vs 'silver foxes' split across keys and miss fuse.
findings.message: ghostreader/analyzers/phrase_thrash.py:174 — Plural phrase keys can diverge. Writers repeating “silver fox” and “silver foxes” can have the repetition split across keys, so the phrase-thrash finding is missed.
